claims.claim: Reviewers describe the original opening prologue featuring Spike and character lore drops as having been removed from the game.

citations.review_text: i was a day one player for this game when it launched. i preordered it on my xbox, and played it non stop for AGES. its so sad to see what the game has become....they removed what was arguably the best part of the game (the prologue), replaced a ton of things with ads, and removed one of my favorite characters (Spike). I 10000% do not reccomend ANYONE buy this game at this point. it feels so lifeless now

As an old returning player coming back to Dying Light 2 after two years away, I am absolutely furious. I bought the game on Steam again to support the developers and experience the story from the beginning, only to discover that Techland has completely gutted the original opening prologue. The walk through the forest mansion with Spike, the Kyle Crane lore drop, and the intense first-night chase are all gone. These weren't meaningless tutorial scenes they were a huge part of the atmosphere, storytelling, and emotional foundation of the game.

What makes this so frustrating is the reasoning behind it. If the goal was to help new players who just want to jump straight into co-op, YOU ALREADY HAD A “SKIP PROLOGUE” BUTTON! Why permanently remove the content instead of simply letting players choose? Anyone who wanted to skip the opening could already do so, while players who actually wanted to experience the story could enjoy it. There was no reason to take that choice away from everyone.

The original prologue also served an important purpose narratively. It built the tension gradually, established the world, gave context to Aiden's journey, and connected the experience to the history of the franchise. Removing that buildup doesn't just make the game shorter it makes the opening feel hollow and creates gaps that hurt the immersion.

I genuinely appreciate the visual upgrades and physics improvements, but it's incredibly frustrating to see those improvements come alongside the removal of content that gave the game character. After supporting Dying Light since the beginning, coming back two years later expecting to relive that experience and finding out that part of it has simply been erased is deeply disappointing.

You didn't need to remove the prologue. You needed to let players choose whether they wanted to skip it.New players could have skipped it, and longtime fans could have experienced the story the way it was originally designed. That choice should never have bee…

citations.review_text:
My first-ever negative review on Steam. Congratulations, Techland. You deserve it.

I genuinely wish I could get a refund.

I bought Dying Light 2 a long time ago, but only recently finished Dying Light 1, including its DLC. And I have to say, Dying Light 1 is an incredible experience, both the base game and The Following. It genuinely feels like a game made with passion.

So I decided to give Dying Light 2 another go, only to discover that the opening was completely different from what I remembered playing about a year ago.

Sure, the graphics look great compared to DL1. But seriously, WHY would you remove the original prologue? And what happened to Spike?!

That opening was one of the most memorable parts of the entire game for me. The atmosphere, the haunting beauty of a world that had fallen apart, the environmental storytelling, the sense of loneliness and wonder, and that emotional connection to the first game through Spike. It was genuinely beautiful. It had soul.

And you just threw it away. For what?

Meanwhile, the game seems increasingly interested in shoving overpriced extras and in-game purchases in players’ faces. What an absolute joke.

You’ve somehow managed to turn a beloved franchise that once felt like a genuine work of art into something that increasingly resembles a soulless, profit-driven live-service cash grab.

Games are supposed to be experiences. They’re supposed to be art. Not just another storefront designed to squeeze money out of players.

The original Dying Light earned my respect. Dying Light 2, and Techland’s decisions surrounding it, have completely destroyed that trust.

I never thought removing an opening chapter could make me lose so much respect for a developer, but here we are.

You’ve ruined something special. I won’t be trusting Techland with another purchase.

the first dying light was better for me. movement in this game doesnt feel as smooth, the hud and gameplay build doesnt feel natural and the parkour feels horrendous compared to the first. 
and my god the consistent ads for dlc and packs in every loading screen is ridiculous and just puts me off... 
Not saying its a terrible game, but it is a massive downgrade from dying light 1

edit:
so ive tried a couple more hours, and i really just cant get motivated with it. the stamina system honestly just feels horrible. it draws so much of your attention that the story and other side quests arent much of a focus. fair play to those that can enjoy DL2, but think my original review stands for me. DL1 felt like such a better game

I like this game, I really do, there is always something to do even in the end game, the story line is good and combat is fluid. 

My biggest problem however is the amount of DLC's, Newsletters, Feedback and AD's they throw into your face. Like NO I don't want to subscribe to your newsletter just to unlock 1 machete just let me do the event and go home.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the parkour mechanics feel inconsistent, with character movements and ledge grabs failing at random points across the map.

citations.review_text: Parkour is pretty bad for a parkour game, why does wall run not work when i have it unlocked, it just makes me jump and fall looking at the wall wishing i was actually on it, EVERY parkour challenge is horribly made cause of this and the checkpoints not working 40 percent of the time, absolute bullshit.

Several years after release and there are still terrible glitches in this game. I teleport to my friends who are trying to talk to an NPC and after that they leave through a door that isn't open for me leaving me trapped inside. It's not a normal door which means I can't open it so I have to wait for my friends to trigger another teleport prompt in order to escape. My friend (who has a better setup than me) experiences random framerate issues. My other friend gets insane visual glitches that are sickening to look at. The PARKOUR, yes the main mechanic of the game, is finicky at seemingly random points of the map. Most often with the bars you swing across.

Meanwhile Techland seems too preoccupied with shoving microtransactions in your face to actually fix them. Fun fact. THE LOADING SCREENS ARE ADS! This is Ubisoft levels of bullshit! Why am I getting ads for your stupid microtransactions whenever I try to load into the campaign? And naturally you have a predatory premium currency instead of just having flat dollar values. Even the store UI is a copy and paste of Call of Duty's.

As a fan of Techland since the Dead Island days this game made me sad on release and after returning I am appalled. I haven't seen The Beast but if this is a sign of Techland's new priorities than maybe I shouldn't bother.

In spite of this game's unacceptable flaws both at release and now I can't say it isn't fun. But man is it frustrating to have to wade through the shit at frequent intervals.

30 hours in, and I just don't want to play anymore.

I finished the original Dying Light twice years ago, and I remember having a great time with it. It wasn't perfect, but I genuinely enjoyed it. So I really wanted to like Dying Light 2. I gave it chance after chance, played for over 30 hours, and kept telling myself it would eventually get better.

But something is missing. Something just feels wrong with this game.

The parkour is one of my biggest frustrations. Sometimes Aiden grabs onto ledges perfectly, and other times he simply refuses to grab onto something that looks completely climbable. It feels inconsistent, and constantly falling, dying, and repeating the same sections becomes exhausting rather than fun.

The nighttime enemies, especially the Volatiles, are another frustration. I understand they're supposed to be dangerous, and I actually loved that feeling in the first game. But here, they're so powerful and encounters with them are so frustrating that nighttime often feels more annoying than exciting.

And then there's the story. I found it weak and uninteresting, and honestly, I struggled to care about what was happening. I'm usually the kind of person who wants to finish story-driven games, even when they're not perfect. But this time, I just can't find the motivation.

That's probably the most disappointing part. The first Dying Light was genuinely fun despite its flaws. This one somehow turns that same experience into frustration and boredom.

I can't even point to one single thing that ruins the game. It's more like a collection of little things that never quite come together. The more I played, the more I felt like I was forcing myself to enjoy something I simply wasn't enjoying.

After 30 hours, I've decided to stop playing. Not because the game is too difficult, but because I'm just not having fun anymore.

Would I recommend it? No, especially not to people hoping to relive what made the original Dying Light so enjoyable.

citations.review_text:
[h1] Dying Light 2 Stay Human [/h1]

[h2] 81/100 [/h2]

Amazing game, riddled with very disgusting tactics, different from Dying Light 1, but not so much

Gotta start by saying that this game, it's really, really good on multiple levels, but in general rule, it's a very good game with some downsides specially at the beginning, and some that are created by straight up corporate greed and disrespect towards the player

 [h3] Starting by the story and characters [/h3] 
The beginning feels a little... Eh, like you're not really interested on it, Hakon is cool but not much else, there's a huge lack of a character that you're interested on and keeps you hooked, Hakon disappears almost immediately, Lawan doesn't appear until you do a good bunch of missions, and... There's just really not many enjoyable characters that you have and engage with throughout the game, on addition to that, Hakon's design being the only one that is likable also it's a problem (Not a big fan of Lawan's design, it just looks... Strange)

Outside of that, halfway throughout the game, this picks up very enjoyably, the story starts picking up more colors (After you exit from the Bazaar zone) and you get a lot more of places to go, also, some characters that appear in the middle are very interesting too, Rowe being one of my absolute favorites despite how short his story was

The story itself on multiple ocassions it's... Very sour, and VERY dark, something that i was not expecting at all for some reason (fun considering that it's Dying Light, and Dying Light 1 is DARK), the death of Rowe, the death of multiple other characters, the way that YOU yourself kill Veronika, it has an extremely dark undertone below it, and that makes it really good and enjoyable, it gives you a sensation that there's a lot on stake, and certain decisions throughout the game help with this, on the sense that, if certain dialogues you pick are not correct, some characters can die, it's a very nice touch, the ending too, leaves…

Well, I'm here from the side of fans of Dying Light series. So...
This part of the series made me upset by the end of the game. The whole story seems pointless to me, idk. This time devs chose a very weird way to tell us a story. 
Poor сharacters. Also, characters who are important to the story have very little screen time, so they don't really feel important. I never really felt any meaningful connection to the characters or got emotionally invested in them. There were some decent attempts at building those connections, but they just weren't enough
Ah, yeah. Just a special part of the game - a very strange political subplot. Yeah, it's people, I understand. And even after 15 years of the apocalypse it's time to play some political games, why not. But this thing doesn't feel like it's supposed to be here, or maybe in another way of storytelling, idk
Throughout the whole game, I felt that almost everything I was doing was pointless. It didn't even bring me closer to my actual goal. And the ending just proved my point. huh.

I think it could have been a more interesting and dramatic story. But it is what it is. 

BUT
what about gameplay - it's great. I love it.
A lot of vertical elements, a lot of tools, pretty cool. 
Vertical gameplay doesn't just exist here, it works really well, and you'll use it throughout the entire game.
Various weapons and upgrades, so you can chop and smash zombies every minute with a different weapon. That's great, and it was my favorite part of the game.
Billions of side quests, but i didn't make them much, so can't say
 much about them

Sooo...
I wouldn't recommend it to those looking for an interesting story.
But I'd recommend it to anyone who wants to spend dozens of hours chopping up zombies and doing side quests. If that's your kind of thing, you'll have a lot of fun

That's it.

amazing game held back by its crashing.

claims.claim: Reviewers express strong dissatisfaction with spatial audio being offered as a paid add-on.

citations.review_text:
It had the potential to be something great. 

Shame they had to ruin it. 

First they started by removing what was widely regarded as one of the strongest parts of the game, removed the introduction to the story, deleted the characters who introduced players to the world, then throw you into a world full of random BS that was actually explained in the bits they removed.

They completely screwed up the colour profiles so everything looked like washed out garbage, or oversaturated garbage (thankfully you can mostly fix it with filters in the nvidia app, or reshade). 

Then they got some AI slop machine to tweak the audio settings, and they want you to pay for through the nose for their tokens that could have been used for something useful instead. Yeah, get bent. I'm not paying £17 just to tweak the audio. I expect scummy moves like that from EA or Ubi, not Techland. 

Have lost all interest in the newer game, won't be buying.

Shame on you guys, you killed the franchise for me.
Trying to charge money for sound quality now? What's next? Extremely predatory and disgusting.

Overall, despite many unpatched glitches and a plethora of animation blunders, it's still a fun game to play, and I generally recommend this product. I will state, however, that I will NOT recommend paying for fake, AI-generated spatial audio. Techland packed an AI retrofit into the game and expects users to pay 1/3 of the game's base retail price for FAKE surround sound, which is absolutely unacceptable. If you're going to charge that much, it needs to be an audio engine overhaul, not just AI slop.
After removing game content, they want you to buy a 20$ dlc that "enhances audio" via AI. No bug fixes. Can't recommend this game right now.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that player choices do not meaningfully impact the narrative or ending cutscenes.

citations.review_text:
While other games will try adding content to keep a playerbase engaged, Dying Light 2 tries the new method of removing content to try and keep payers engaged which I can't say is a good strategy. They make a new stamina system for this game? and then backtrack it almost immediately when there were some growing pains. The player base isn't engaging with one of the two main factions because some people were jaded by the very reasonable response of killing someone that is on the verge of turning inside of your camp? just fade it to black instead so that it makes no sense when that exact scene is then referenced in dialogue still. and fuck it, remove the intro too while you are at it.

So, I will not rag on the story too much, because as a series that is a spiritual successor to Dead Island, and it wasn't even a main focus of Dying Light 1, story was never what we were here for. WHAT I WILL rag  on though is the fact that the idea that your choices make a difference is a lie because it doesn't work. I did two playthroughs with vastly different choices in each and got the exact same cutscene regardless.

Combat also feels less crunchy in my opinion in this game but that might just be the audio in my own personal preferences, but there is some improvements to the parkour system overall. When it does the input you are trying to do because you have everything binded to the same thing.

Now, you might ask why I have so many hours in a game I hate?

Well, I have the unfortunate tism of Achievement Hunting and there is an achievement for running, specifically running 960km in game, and given the fact you have a glider in this game I was using that instead, and across 2 playthroughs, I barely even breached 300km. And I was not going to justify another playthrough of this game for that.
So I tried to idle with a rubber band on my controller. BUT THE GAME RECOGNISES THIS AND INSTEAD PAUSES AFTER 5 MINUTES. SO EITHER YOU SET UP A MACRO, OR YOU PLAYTHROUGH THE BORING ASS G…

The game is overall Okay, except that the main story is ridiculously bad, especially everything that happens during last mission doesn't have any logic and sense whatsoever. Last hour of the game is just a one big long lasting facepalm from the narrative and story perspective. Prequel had much stronger storytelling in this regard.

Also have to point out that I didn't notice any meaningful changes to the world by player's plot choices - probably this part of game mechanics was ruined when Avelon left the team, sadly.

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering various technical bugs and glitches, such as raining indoors, enemies remaining stuck in locations, and erratic hitboxes on parkour challenges.

citations.review_text: The variety and type of missions in Dying Light 2 is reminiscent of DL but better. One bug is that it rains indoors. This game also requires a better than average rig to get the best performance out of it and my 9700k struggles.

If you're a sort of person who doesn't give a f about a story then this game is good. Messing around in the city is very fun.

That being said the fact that after 4 years they still didn't fix the bugs is unacceptable. Right now it's impossible to finish the game without having to work around the glitches. Let's list what I encountered, shall we?
- Some loot places have phantom zombies which you can't hit or aggro.
- Question marks on the map doesn't disappear at times. Restarting the game doesn't fix it.
- After restarting the challenge the screen can get "squeezed down" and you have to restart the game to literally see anything.
- Big police cars can't be opened even though the interaction marker is there.
- Interaction points get stuck under the ground making them unreachable.
- Interaction points can have wrong offsets making them float somewhere in the air instead of being on the interactible object.
- There is a sidequest in which you talk on a radio with a mysterious person. The problem is the subtitles have their name next to the caption which spoils the whole "wow" effect of who that mysterious person is.
- Parkour challenges' circles have arbitrary hitboxes, smaller than the visuals suggest. It's incredibly infuriating when you go through the circle but it doesn't count because you apparently didn't go as close to the circle center as devs intended.
- Monkey bars are incredibly unreliable and buggy. Sometimes you jump downwards, sometimes you jump forward, sometimes you don't jump at all.

Add to that the microtransaction hellhole in a fully priced, singleplayer game and there you are - a freshly made *fuck you* downvote from me.

I liked this game more than the first title in the series.

Some people might disagree, but the complexity of certain mechanics, the story choices, and other aspects made me love it.

The quality of life has improved significantly throughout the updates, making the game much better than its predecessor.

With the latest updates, we also got community maps and mods, making the game much more mod-friendly.

Like any game, it isn't perfect. Some of its flaws include:

Inconsistencies in the story's narrative.

A lot of annoying glitches:

Encounter glitches.

Weapon glitches.

XP glitches.

Lack of an efficient mass-dismantling system (especially in a game where every resource matters).

Inefficient fast-travel system.

Sketchy grappling hook mechanics.

An excessively grindy Tower Raid mode.

Bolters that are way too slow and easy to catch, and don't run toward Volatiles.

Overall, I loved the combat, the new parkour abilities, the new enemy types, the encounters, and much more. I would strongly recommend playing it if you enjoy the series or the genre.

(I know I've listed quite a few negatives, but they're mostly things you can overlook or adapt to.)
